events.credibility_reason: Rests on Mochizuki's IUT framework, where Scholze and Stix located a specific gap (IUT III, Thm 3.11 to Cor 3.12). The July 2026 LANA interim report says the same step is still unresolved. No independent reader of the Vojta-inequality claim after about 31 months. Joshi is an established arithmetic geometer and disputes the objections, so this is doubtful rather than set aside.

Scholze and Stix identified a specific gap in a key step. Mochizuki disputes it, and nobody neutral has adjudicated. The LANA interim report finds an unresolved compatibility problem at the same step.
Effective versions conditional on IUT's disputed non-effective Vojta/abc claims. Journal acceptance by Kodai does not resolve the Scholze-Stix gap upstream.
Relies on the disputed IUT framework.
Single-author math.GM preprint, and its content is known only through a third-party summary. It proves a weaker (1 - epsilon) gap inequality under a positivity hypothesis.

why: The statement asks for Vojta's general height inequality over number fields. Only results that prove that inequality for a restricted class of varieties or divisors count as a case. I scored the claimed IUT inequality for P^1 minus three points with bounded-degree points as a case, in both Joshi's 2024 version and Mochizuki's 2021 version: it is Vojta's inequality for one curve and divisor, and van Frankenhuysen's equivalence makes it the abc-type case. Both stay unreviewed and doubtful because of the specific Scholze-Stix gap, which the other side still disputes. I did not set them aside because established authors contest the gap and nobody has conceded it. Yasufuku's unconditional result for a family of rational surfaces is also a pre-snapshot case. Everything else is a variant: function-field, complex or non-Archimedean analogues, integral-point or Bombieri-Lang siblings, truncated counting functions, weaker gap inequalities, effective abc, and Levin's unbounded-degree counterexample. A few events prove nothing about the statement and are none: a conjecture formulation, a conditional application, a re-proof of Mordell-Faltings, a talk listing and the LANA formalisation report. No AI system is credited in any event.
doubts: Close call: whether Joshi's inequality, in Mochizuki's normalisation, for compactly bounded sets of bounded-degree points over Q-bar, is exactly a special case of the stated conjecture or a restated variant. I read it as a case because of the cited equivalence with abc. The Tiebekabe content comes only from a third-party summary. I marked the Fesenko et al. Kodai paper digested on journal acceptance even though it is conditional on disputed IUT results. The AI negatives rest on partial reads of the full texts.
